author: Zane Douglas
title: Rogers boys hockey stunned in semifinals - NewsBreak
text:
By Zane Douglas ,
13 hours ago After a 21 win season that saw a peak of beating Minnetonka, Rogers fell in the semifinals in the 6AA boys hockey tournament on Feb. 21 to the four seed Wayzata 5-2.
The Royals lost 5-2 against the Trojans after the Trojans got off to a 4-0 start in the first two periods, ending the 21-win season for the Royals.
Senior forward Eli Molde was the star of the show for Wayzata, totaling a hat trick and adding an assist. Molde scored two of his goals consecutively in the first and second periods as the team's second and third goal.
Trojan senior forward Christopher Pyle added a goal and two assists of his own, both assists being to Molde. Molde's third goal was scored empty net with four minutes left and Rogers down 4-1.
The Royals scored early into the third period to finally get on the board thanks to senior forward Cole Bumgarner. Senior defenseman Blake Sinclair and forward Avenir Belous assisted on the goal.
Late game after the Trojans had made it 5-1, the Royals scored one more time. Belous was assisted by senior forwards Brayden Lorentzen and Brock Cheslock.
The star of the game was Trojan goalie Ryan Pellinger. The senior faced 46 shots on goal and was able to keep Rogers to two goals, both in the third period. Wayzata will play Edina in the section finals for a chance at state.
Bumgarner and Cheslock led the Royals in points on the season with 55 each. Bumgarner led the team with 32 assists. Cheslock scored 34 goals to lead the team on that front.
The Royals hadn't lost a game since Dec. 6 against Hill-Murray 1-0. The team's season ended on Feb. 21 finishing with a 21-5-1 record.
